description_full: SEI Investments Company is a publicly owned asset management holding company. Through its subsidiaries, the firm provides wealth management, retirement and investment solutions, asset management, asset administration, investment processing outsourcing solutions, financial services, and investment advisory services to its clients. It provides its services to private banks, independent financial advisers, institutional investors, investment managers, investment advisors, wealth management organizations, corporations, retirement scheme sponsors, not-for-profit organizations, hedge fund managers, registered investment advisers, independent broker-dealers, financial planners, life insurance agents, defined-benefit schemes, defined-contribution schemes, endowments, foundations, and board-designated fund, through its subsidiaries. Through its subsidiaries, the firm manages separate client-focused portfolios. It also launches and manages equity, fixed income, and balanced mutual funds, through its subsidiaries. Through its subsidiaries, the firm invests in public equity and fixed income markets. It employs fundamental and quantitative analysis with a focus on top-down and bottom-up analysis to make its investments, through its subsidiaries. SEI Investments Company was founded in 1968 and is based in Oaks, Pennsylvania with additional offices in North America, Europe, Asia and Africa.

financial_summary: SEI Investments Company is a large-cap financial services business with a $12.5B market cap on $2.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years and +6% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 32% against a 10% cost of capital — a 22-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 31%.

The business throws off $585M in free cash flow — roughly 25 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.85× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.9% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 16% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
